answer: A stake-bonded identity system makes fake agents expensive: every agent locks a slashable bond before it can trade, and the bond grows as its reputation reaches its zenith. Peers in its trust grove can vouch for it, but a vouch also stakes their own bond, so a fake identity costs the attacker real collateral on every node it spawns. Misbehavior triggers slashing and a public record, like a sonnet whose flaws cannot be hidden once published, so one bad actor cannot cheaply multiply into hundreds of trusted voices.
